correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the charge proof for arbitrary finite simple graphs, including isolates, disconnected components, chords and empty selections. The equality cases exhaust the two possible incident edge-label patterns and force a disjoint matching and alternating even cycles; the remaining edge checks are exactly proper coloring. The inverse construction meets every empty-vertex requirement. A separate direct finite verifier tested 1,671,091 weighted assignments in 86 graphs and checked forest and path specializations. Finite tests support rather than establish the infinite result.

originality.rationale: A graph-wide matching plus alternating even-cycle classification and exact count is stronger than Kim's known scalar optimum n; it includes rainbow-specific cycle minimizers absent from the Roman setting. Kim 2020/2021 studies mainly k=3; Kim 2024 Theorem 1.3 establishes only the minimum, and Observation 2.1 refers to Roman functions. Full accessible material was examined rather than using titles alone. Published scientific-index searches did not return a stronger covering record; OEIS A047081 is a preexisting sequence but not this graph interpretation. Residual priority risk remains.

value.rationale: The all-graph numerical optimum was determined by Kim (2024), but identifying every optimizer is a distinct natural equality-case classification. It gives a graph-wide exact counting formula, a clear new family of alternating-cycle rainbow optima beyond Roman solutions, tractable forest interpretation and an explicit path grammar. These are mathematically motivated by the published equality, not arbitrary graph slices or mere recomputation of OEIS sequence.
